theme: Covenant renewed; the law rewritten; Moses’ face shines
readingInstruction: Read Exodus 34:1-35:35. After the golden calf, the covenant is renewed. This is the other side of the story, and one of the most important statements of God’s character in the Old Testament. Read the proclamation of his name in 34:6-7 slowly, and notice how often the rest of the Bible returns to it.
settingTheScene: Moses has interceded, and God has agreed to go with Israel. Now Moses is called back up the mountain with two new stone tablets. This time God does not simply give the commands. He proclaims his own name and character first. Then he renews the covenant, and Moses comes down with a face that shines. Chapter 35 begins the account of building the tabernacle, after the long set of instructions. The people respond with overflowing generosity.
observation: God tells Moses to cut two tablets “like the first,” and he will write on them himself (34:1).
“The LORD passed before him and proclaimed, The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness” (34:6).
God continues: “keeping steadfast love for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, but who will by no means clear the guilty” (34:7).
Moses bows and worships at once, and asks God to go with them and pardon their iniquity (34:8-9).
God warns against making covenants with the people of the land and against idolatry (34:11-17).
Moses stays on the mountain forty days and nights, and writes “the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments” (34:28).
Moses’ face shines so brightly that the people are afraid, and he puts a veil over it when he is not speaking with God (34:29-35).
In chapter 35, the people bring gifts “every one whose heart stirred him, and everyone whose spirit moved him” (35:21), and the response is so great that Moses has to tell them to stop (36:5-7).
interpretation:
Exodus 34:6-7 is the center of the passage and one of the most quoted verses in the Old Testament. It is the answer to Moses’ prayer, “Show me your glory.” God’s glory, it turns out, is his character: mercy, grace, patience, love, and faithfulness. The list begins with mercy and ends with justice, and every word is deliberate. God forgives sin, and he does not ignore it.

The proclamation is repeated throughout the Bible. David uses it in Psalm 86:15 and 103:8. Joel quotes it in Joel 2:13, and Jonah complains about it: “I knew that you are a gracious God and merciful” (Jonah 4:2). It is a creed that Israel returned to again and again. When they sinned, they remembered who God is.

Look at what comes right after the proclamation. Moses bows down and prays. He does not argue. He worships and asks for pardon. The same man who was bold on behalf of the people is now humble in the presence of God’s glory. The two postures belong together.

The renewed covenant shows grace at work. God could have ended things at the calf. Instead he cuts new tablets, with Moses doing the carving and God doing the writing. The broken covenant is mended, not because Israel has earned it, but because God is merciful.

The shining face is a sign that anyone who spends time in God’s presence is changed. Moses does not know his face is shining (34:29). He has been with God, and it shows. The veil is for the sake of the people, who cannot bear to look. Paul will make much of this in 2 Corinthians 3.

Finally, the people’s generosity in chapters 35 and 36 is the fitting response. They give so much that Moses has to tell them to stop. Forgiven people give freely.
connection: Paul compares Moses’ veiled face with the unveiled glory of Christ. “And we all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another” (2 Corinthians 3:18). John writes that the Word was “full of grace and truth” (John 1:14), using the words of Exodus 34:6. Jesus is the full revelation of God’s glory (Hebrews 1:3), and the Father’s steadfast love is shown in him.
application:
Memorize Exodus 34:6-7, or at least the first half. Return to it when you doubt God’s goodness.

Ask what it would mean for you to spend time with God so that others notice a change in you.

If God has forgiven you something, ask how you can respond with generosity this week.
prayerPrompts: Praise God as merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in love.
Thank him for forgiving you in Christ.
Ask him to change you by your time with him and to make you generous.
